name: Data analysis
summary: Turn messy numbers into answers a business can act on.
skills: Cleaning data, formulas, pivot tables and simple charts.
Pulling the data you need out of a database.
Building a dashboard people can read at a glance.
Saying what the numbers mean and what to do next, in plain words.
learn: Short, interactive SQL lessons that run in your browser.
Short Python, pandas and data visualisation courses.
questions: Tell me about a time you found something unexpected in data.
Say what you noticed, how you checked it was real, and what changed because of it.
How do you clean a messy dataset?
Walk through your order: duplicates, blanks, wrong formats, outliers. Say why each one matters.
What is the difference between a VLOOKUP and a pivot table?
One finds a value, the other summarises many rows. Give a real example of each.
How would you explain a chart to someone who hates numbers?
Lead with the one message. Show that you think about your audience.

name: Accounting
summary: Keep a business's money records accurate and on time.
skills: Recording transactions and keeping ledgers correct.
Matching the books to bank and M-Pesa statements.
Reading and preparing an income statement and balance sheet.
QuickBooks, Sage or similar, plus strong spreadsheets.
learn: Plain explanations of core accounting topics.
Free lessons on statements and business finance.
Free guides on accounting and Excel.
questions: How would you handle a bank reconciliation that doesn't balance?
Show your method: timing differences, missing entries, then errors.
What is the difference between cash and accrual accounting?
Explain when income and costs are recorded, with a simple example.
A manager asks you to backdate an invoice. What do you do?
Say no politely, explain why, and offer the correct way.
How do you avoid mistakes when work piles up at month end?
Talk about checklists, order of work and checking your own numbers.

name: Finance
summary: Help a business decide what it can afford and what is worth doing.
skills: Planning income and costs, and tracking against the plan.
Knowing when money comes in and goes out.
Building a clear spreadsheet to test a decision.
Giving a clear answer, not just a table of numbers.
learn: Free guides on modelling and analysis.
questions: How would you decide if a business should buy a new machine?
Compare the cost with the extra profit, work out payback time, then state a view.
What is the difference between profit and cash flow?
A business can show a profit and still run out of cash. Give an example.
Which numbers would you check first in a small business?
Name a few, such as cash, margin and debtors, and say why.
Tell me about a time your numbers changed a decision.
A university project works. Say what the decision was and how you influenced it.

name: Digital marketing
summary: Find the right customers online and turn their attention into sales.
skills: Working out who buys, and what makes them act.
Clear messages, simple design, short video.
Setting up Meta and Google ads on a small budget.
Using analytics to see what worked and what to stop.
learn: Free training and certificates for Google Ads and Analytics.
Free training on Facebook and Instagram ads.
questions: You have KSh 10,000 to promote a small shop. What do you do?
Choose one goal and one audience, then say how you would measure it.
Tell me about a campaign you admire. Why did it work?
Pick a Kenyan brand if you can. Explain the idea, not just that you liked it.
Which numbers tell you a campaign is working?
Go past likes. Talk about clicks, cost per lead and sales.
An ad gets many likes but no sales. What do you check?
Audience, offer, landing page, then how easy it is to buy.

name: Software development
summary: Build software that works, and explain how you built it.
skills: JavaScript or Python is a good place to start.
Saving your work and collaborating on code.
Finding the cause of a problem instead of guessing.
learn: A free path through web development.
The trusted reference for HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
questions: Walk me through something you built.
Cover the problem, your choices, what broke and what you would change.
How do you debug something you don't understand?
Reproduce it, narrow it down, read the error, test one idea at a time.
What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL databases?
Explain each in a sentence, then say when you would use it.
How do you use AI tools when you code?
Be honest. Show that you check and understand what they produce.

name: Sales
summary: Understand what people need and help them say yes.
skills: Knowing who to approach and how to reach them.
Responding calmly to 'it's too expensive' or 'not now'.
Keeping records and staying in touch.
learn: Free short courses on sales and negotiation.
questions: Sell me this pen.
Ask what I need first, then link the pen to that need.
A customer says your price is too high. What do you say?
Ask what they are comparing it with, then talk about value.
Tell me about a time you persuaded someone.
Any real story works. Say what they wanted and how you got there.
How do you handle being told no all day?
Be honest, and show how you learn from it and keep going.

name: Customer service
summary: Solve people's problems and keep them coming back.
skills: Replies that are polite, short and correct.
Handling an angry customer without taking it personally.
Finding the actual issue and fixing it.
Logging issues so nobody has to explain twice.
learn: Free short courses on customer care and communication.
questions: A customer is shouting at you. What do you do?
Listen, acknowledge, apologise for the problem, and give a next step.
What makes good customer service?
Use an example of when a business treated you well.
How do you handle a problem you can't solve yourself?
Tell the customer what happens next, escalate it, and follow up.
Tell me about a time you helped someone who was upset.
Use a real story from school, church, a shop or home.

name: IT support
summary: Keep people's computers and networks working.
skills: Working step by step from symptom to cause.
IP addresses, routers, Wi-Fi and DNS.
Accounts, updates, email and common faults.
Helping non-technical people without talking down to them.
learn: Free introductory networking and IT courses.
Free video courses for CompTIA A+ and Network+.
Free training on Windows and Microsoft 365.
questions: A user says the internet is down. What do you check first?
Is it one person or everyone? Then cable, Wi-Fi, IP, router, provider.
How would you explain DNS to a non-technical person?
A phone book for the internet works well.
What would you do if a computer gets a virus?
Disconnect it, scan it, recover the data, and find how it got in.
How do you handle many urgent requests at once?
Say how you decide what comes first, and how you keep people informed.

name: Graphic design
summary: Make ideas clear and attractive, and explain why they work.
skills: Choosing and combining them with purpose.
Canva, Photoshop, Illustrator, Figma or CorelDRAW.
Designing for the client's goal, not your own taste.
questions: Walk me through one piece of your work.
Start with the goal and the audience, then explain your choices.
A client says, 'Make the logo bigger.' What do you do?
Find the real concern behind the request, and show options.
How do you take criticism of your work?
Show that you separate yourself from the work and ask useful questions.
Design a poster for a kiosk with no budget. Where do you start?
Message first, audience second, tools last.

name: Content writing
summary: Write words people actually read and act on.
skills: Short sentences, plain words, no padding.
Getting facts right and using reliable sources.
Basic SEO, so people can find the page.
Cutting your own work and fixing it.
questions: How do you write about a topic you know nothing about?
Explain how you research, check facts and find the angle.
How do you change your writing for different readers?
Compare two examples, such as a boda rider and a bank manager.
How do you use AI tools in your writing?
Be honest. Say how you check facts and keep your own voice.
Someone rewrites your work heavily. How do you react?
Ask what they changed and why, then use it next time.

name: Social media
summary: Build an audience for a brand and turn it into customers.
skills: Deciding what to post, when and why.
Filming and editing for TikTok and Reels.
Replying to comments and messages in the brand's voice.
Tracking what grows the business, not just likes.
learn: Free training for Facebook and Instagram.
Free lessons on making social graphics.
questions: Plan a week of posts for a local salon.
Mix types: results, tips, behind the scenes, an offer. Say why.
A post gets an angry comment. What do you do?
Reply quickly and calmly, take it to DMs, and don't delete fair complaints.
Which brand in Kenya does social media well?
Name one, and say what they do that you would copy.
How do you know social media is helping the business?
Link it to leads, bookings or sales.

name: Human resources
summary: Help a business hire, look after and keep good people.
skills: Writing job ads, shortlisting fairly, running interviews.
The basics of contracts, leave and termination.
Keeping personal information accurate and private.
Listening, staying fair and keeping confidence.
learn: Search for the Employment Act and read it at the source.
Free short courses on human resources.
Free courses from The Open University.
questions: How would you shortlist 200 applications fairly?
Set criteria before you read, and score each person the same way.
An employee tells you something in confidence about a manager. What do you do?
Listen, explain the limits of confidentiality, and follow the process.
What should every employment contract include?
Role, pay, hours, leave, notice period, and start date.
How would you make a new employee's first week go well?
Talk about preparation, introductions, and clear first tasks.

name: Office administration
summary: Keep an office organised so everyone else can do their job.
skills: Managing calendars, files, meetings and deadlines.
Handling people and confidential information with care.
learn: Free short courses on office administration.
questions: Your boss gives you three urgent jobs at once. What do you do?
Ask what comes first, and say what can wait.
How do you keep track of many deadlines?
Show your real system, even if it is simple.
A visitor arrives angry and without an appointment. What do you do?
Stay calm, listen, and find the right person or time.
How do you take meeting minutes?
Capture decisions, actions, owners and dates, not every word.

name: Procurement
summary: Buy the right things at the right price, honestly.
skills: Looking at price, quality, delivery and reliability.
Knowing how tendering works in Kenya.
learn: Kenya's public procurement regulator: laws and guidance.
Free short courses on procurement and supply chains.
questions: How would you choose between three suppliers?
Set your criteria first, score each one, and explain the trade-offs.
A supplier offers you a gift. What do you do?
Decline, report it, and follow company policy.
A delivery arrives late and incomplete. What are your next steps?
Record it, contact the supplier, tell users, and review the contract.
How can a company save money without lowering quality?
Talk about combining orders, negotiation, and total cost.

name: Logistics
summary: Get goods to the right place, on time, at a sensible cost.
skills: Making the best use of vehicles and time.
Knowing what you have and when to reorder.
Dealing with breakdowns, delays and shortages.
learn: Free short courses on logistics and supply chains.
Free courses from The Open University.
questions: A lorry breaks down with urgent orders on board. What do you do?
Sort out safety first, tell customers, find another vehicle, then review.
How would you plan deliveries to 30 shops with two lorries?
Group shops by area, consider load limits, then schedule by priority.
How do you stop stock running out?
Talk about reorder levels and regular counts.
Which costs would you track in a delivery business?
Fuel, maintenance, driver time and failed deliveries.
